compatibility_matrix.details: Bulk JSON is an array of triples [operational certificate text envelope, VRF signing-key text envelope, KES signing-key text envelope]. Each envelope is decoded into a file-backed PraosCredentialsUnsound; singleton and bulk credentials are concatenated. Bulk parsing does not perform the singleton opcert/KES-key hash check.
--shelley-operational-certificate, --shelley-vrf-key and --shelley-kes-key must all be present or all absent. The key and certificate hot-key hashes are checked for equality.

--shelley-kes-agent-socket replaces --shelley-kes-key, still requires certificate and VRF. The loader reads the certificate cold verification key but does not check its hot key against the agent-delivered key. A dynamic hot key and receiver are constructed.
The inspected decoder expects triples, not object entries; versioned file and agent objects are planned integration, not existing baseline forms. Shelley/Credentials.hs is absent in this checkout.

The bulk decoder accepts triples of text envelopes only; it has no agent source branch. A historical installed-node preflight rejected an agent-shaped object with 'expected Array, but encountered Object'; that binary's dirty-source/build identity was not established.

reload_source_observations.initialization_boundary: On UNIX the initial handler updates topology and RPC and traces BlockForgingUpdate NotEffective; after consensus initialization the node-kernel hook installs the handler that calls updateBlockForging.
reload_source_observations.configured_paths: updateBlockForging calls mkConsensusProtocol with ncProtocolConfig and ncProtocolFiles from the original NodeConfiguration; it rereads those configured credential paths, not new CLI paths. A matching block type yields new forging workers passed to setBlockForging.
reload_source_observations.malformed_or_invalid: Bulk JSON decode produces EnvelopeParseError; invalid embedded envelopes produce FileError with synthetic bulk index/type location; singleton incomplete credentials or mismatched KES key yield explicit errors. Except for the missing-file cases below, updateBlockForging traces BlockForgingUpdateError without installing a replacement forging set. Block-type mismatch is also traced without setBlockForging.
reload_source_observations.missing_and_io: For Shelley and Cardano protocol wrappers, singleton credential FileError FileDoesNotExistError causes setBlockForging [] and DisabledBlockForging. For the Cardano wrapper, every bulk CredentialsReadError is mapped to FileDoesNotExistError regardless of the underlying IO error and likewise disables the entire forging set. For a Shelley wrapper, CredentialsReadError is not mapped by wasFileRemovedFromScope and is traced as an update error instead. Malformed bulk JSON is not a CredentialsReadError. Agent socket connection errors occur asynchronously and are not credential-file read errors.
reload_source_observations.file_and_agent_lifecycle: File credentials initialize a hot key; slot-driven evolution catches up in memory subject to validity. An agent constructs a keyless dynamic hot key and receiver; ordinary disconnect retains the existing key unless an explicit Drop is received. Explicit reload replaces workers and can leave an unavailable replacement keyless until a fresh delivery. These are source/design observations, not proof of a live reload.

cancellation_evidence.inspected_source_hazard: runKESAgentClient catches AsyncCancelled inside forever, catches SomeException too, and delays ten seconds before retrying. HotKey.mkHotKeyWith finalizes with cancel keyThreadAsync followed by unset. A swallowed cancellation can prevent awaited cancellation and therefore cleanup; both exception handlers require cancellation-aware treatment.

prior_isolated_probe.description: An in-memory Haskell probe using io-classes 1.10.1.0 reproduced the exception-loop structure: cancellation was caught, the loop re-entered after ten seconds and waiting cancellation did not complete. It was not the actual native receiver/finalizer.
